subject.title: Telegram detached subagents can run silently without liveness or terminal notification

question: Should OpenClaw solve #101656 as a generic runtime/session activity contract consumed by Telegram, or as a Telegram-only liveness workaround?
rationale: The requested behavior crosses runtime task state, requester-session delivery, Telegram UX, status command semantics, and non-sensitive metadata policy, so automation should not choose the permanent product boundary by itself.

options.title: Generic activity substrate first
options.body: Implement or align with a gateway/runtime-owned metadata surface, then add Telegram rendering for liveness and terminal states.

options.title: Telegram-only workaround
options.body: Add channel-local typing and heartbeat behavior sooner, but risk duplicating or drifting from session/task truth as #39127 and #97963 evolve.

options.title: Defer to broader observability work
options.body: Keep this issue blocked on #39127/#38626 and only revisit Telegram-specific UX after the generic activity API lands.

recommendation.title: Generic activity substrate first
recommendation.body: Implement or align with a gateway/runtime-owned metadata surface, then add Telegram rendering for liveness and terminal states.

likelyOwner.reason: Most active recent contributor across the implicated Telegram, task, status, and subagent delivery surfaces.
